source_documents.title: Hydration-Gated Photoinduced Electron Transfer in BODIPY Dyes

reference_evidence_units.quote: In more polar media, fluorescence is progressively quenched: in dichloromethane ΦF decreases to 0.072, and in acetonitrile ΦF drops to 0.006, consistent with efficient PET driven by dielectric stabilization of the formed CT state [34].
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dyad 1 is strongly emissive in nonpolar solvents and quenched in polar solvents, attributed to PET to a CT state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Efficient PET is observed in 1 in polar solvents (Table 1) despite modest endergonicity (ΔG°PET = +0.14 eV), consistent with prior reports [39].
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Electrochemical driving force for PET in dyad 1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the corresponding F‐BODIPY‐based dyads 1–4, charge recombination from the CT state populated the triplet manifold via spin–orbit charge‐transfer intersystem crossing (SOCT‐ISC) [49].
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyads 1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Charge recombination of the CT state of the F-BODIPY dyads populates the triplet via SOCT-ISC.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Cited from the authors' earlier work [49]; not re-measured for dyad 1 here.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Polar-solvent quenching of dyad 1 is attributed to PET from anthracene to BODIPY.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: CT recombination populates the triplet by SOCT-ISC (from the authors' previous work).
